reasons: plugin/gate/checks.py: dropped_eval_cases's new `dot_dropped` set (introduced by this exact round's fix) is unioned into the result unconditionally -- `dropped = set(dot_dropped) | {...filtered by survivor_cases...}` -- never filtered against `survivor_cases`. So when one file of a multi-file eval case is renamed to a dot-prefixed destination while a sibling file in the same, original (visible) case folder is left untouched, the whole case is reported as a drop even though the sibling still exists and is visible at HEAD. Traced with real `tree_files` semantics (git ls-tree lists every blob, dot-prefixed or not, so the sibling's path, e.g. `evals/cases/foo/b.yaml`, is genuinely a survivor and `case_of()` maps it back to `foo`): the source case name still lands in `survivor_cases`, yet the unconditional `set(dot_dropped)` union reports it dropped anyway.

This directly contradicts the design invariant both spec.md ('A case is dropped when no path remains, at HEAD's committed tree, under its folder ... so that one file dropped out of a multi-file case while a sibling survives is never mistaken for the whole case's drop') and plan.md's Risks section state for this exact function -- the invariant is honored for a plain `D` (proven by `test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop`) but not for a dot-prefixed rename of one file in a multi-file case, which has no test at all.

This is a false-positive in the gate's own deterministic ratchets check (the subject of this whole change), which runs at phases (c)/(d)/(e) for every change, in every project the plugin drives (intent.md's own 'Affected users and systems' -- wide blast radius). A legitimate partial reorganisation of a multi-file eval case that happens to dot-rename one file would incorrectly park the change on an undeclared 'ratchet: evals' hit for the whole case, not just the renamed file.

Confirmed this is newly introduced by the code under review, not a pre-existing accepted gap: before this round's fix there was no separate `dot_dropped` set at all (the owner's bug report was about the destination also being added to `touched`); the fix replaced that with a `dot_dropped` set that bypasses the same survivor-based filtering `touched` otherwise goes through, which is what creates the gap.

No existing or added test exercises this scenario (a dot-rename of one case file alongside an untouched, surviving sibling in the same source case folder), so the whole suite (including this round's own two targeted fixes) passes with this bug present -- angle 6 (the tests) finds nothing here that would catch it.
classification_reasons: Wide blast radius: `check_ratchets` is wired into CHECKS_BY_PHASE for (c), (d) and (e) and runs on every change, in every project the plugin drives, per intent.md -- not a small, local change.
The code under review is new gate/check logic (not covered by pre-existing tests), and this round's fix itself modifies that logic's eval-case drop rule.
No schema or migration, but the change does alter deterministic-gate behavior that other automation (owner's accept-risk label, PR conformance line) depends on.
attempted: Intent: confirmed the two fixes match exactly what the owner's review comments (evidence/fix-requests.json, 2026-10-16T18:21:37Z and 11:27:25Z) asked for, and nothing beyond that scope was silently changed.

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md's eval-case drop rule and plan.md's Risks/Proof sections; traced `dropped_eval_cases` line by line against both the owner's test fixture and a realistic live-git scenario; found the dot-rename path does not honor the survivor-based 'sibling survives is not a drop' invariant the spec states for this same function, even though the sibling-survives invariant is honored for the plain-delete path and has its own passing test.

Proof: compared the current `plugin/gate/checks.py: dropped_eval_cases` and `tests/test_gate.py::test_dropped_test_files_and_eval_cases_pure` / `test_gate_continues_on_a_clean_change` against the diff; both targeted fixes are correctly implemented and verified by re-deriving the test's expected values by hand (the dot-rename-destination-as-its-own-case bug is gone; the expected-check-name-set test now includes 'ratchets'). No test.log/build.log/lint.log exist yet at phase (c) (expected per the brief); verifier.md and gate-c.json were read for context only, not cited as proof of the diff's correctness -- my own trace of the function against both the unit-test fixture and a constructed live-git scenario is the basis for the finding above.

Blast radius: `check_ratchets` runs at (c)/(d)/(e) in every project; traced `tree_files`'s real semantics (plugin/gate/diff.py tree_files uses `git ls-tree`, which does not exclude dot-prefixed paths) to confirm the false-positive scenario is reachable in a real repository, not just an artifact of the synthetic unit-test fixture.
Policies: no security-baseline, data-conventions or guardrail-file issue found; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) appears in the diff.

The tests: searched the whole test suite for other 'expected check-name set' assertions that might now be stale after adding `ratchets` to CHECKS_BY_PHASE['c']/['d']/['e'] (grep for `set(_names(result, True)) ==` and for the string 'ratchets' across tests/); found exactly one other such exhaustive-set test, at phase (b), which correctly does not include ratchets (phase (b) is excluded by design) -- no other stale assertion found. Verified the dot-rename gap is untested by searching for every `dropped_eval_cases`/`dot_rename`/`eval_case` test name in tests/test_gate.py.
